item.title: Networking
item.description:
Considerations of Peer-to-Peer Communication 🔗

When two people open the same design, their browsers exchange edits directly over WebRTC. Layer5 Cloud takes part only at the start and for presence. Edits do not pass through Layer5 Cloud or Meshery Server.

A self-hosted provider is its own signaling host. Browsers open a WebSocket to /collaboration on your deployment. Users connected to your deployment never signal through Layer5’s hosted service, and there is no public Layer5 signaling server to point them at.

item.title: Identity Services
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud offers a built-in identity provider (IDP), supporting OIDC for normal users and token-based authentication (access, ID, refresh tokens) for API clients with JSON Web Signature (JWS) for token signing. Layer5 Cloud users can sign-up via email and password in addition to social identity providers (Google and GitHub) via OAuth2. See Getting Started with a Layer5 Account for details.

Layer5 Cloud identity services include account recovery, email verification, and social sign-in with Google and GitHub. Password sign-in is on, with a minimum of 8 characters, a check against known-breached passwords, and a rejection when the password is too similar to the account identifier.

item.title: Monitoring
item.description:
Layer5 Cloud gives you health endpoints, structured logs with stable error codes, startup messages, and optional OpenTelemetry traces. It does not expose a Prometheus metrics endpoint. Build service-level indicators from your ingress and Kubernetes metrics plus the signals below.

Objectives 🔗

  • Know whether the process is running (/healthz) and whether startup finished (/readyz)
  • Alert on stable error codes, not on message text
  • Turn tracing on only when you have a collector
  • Keep startup logs secret, because provider initialization logs the initial administrator password
